verses: لَعَلَّكَ بَٰخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا۟ مُؤْمِنِينَ
إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ ءَايَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَٰقُهُمْ لَهَا خَٰضِعِينَ
وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ
فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا۟ فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنۢبَٰٓؤُا۟ مَا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ
إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱئْتِ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ
فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ
وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذًا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِى رَبِّى حُكْمًا وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَىَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ
قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ
قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَٰهًا غَيْرِى لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ
قَالَ فَأْتِ بِهِۦٓ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ
وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ
قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ
قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ ٱلسَّحَرَةَ إِن كَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
فَلَمَّا جَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ قَالُوا۟ لِفِرْعَوْنَ أَئِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَّمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰٓ أَلْقُوا۟ مَآ أَنتُم مُّلْقُونَ
فَأَلْقَوْا۟ حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا۟ بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
فَأَلْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ

قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
قَالُوا۟ لَا ضَيْرَ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ
إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَآ أَن كُنَّآ أَوَّلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِىٓ إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ
فَلَمَّا تَرَٰٓءَا ٱلْجَمْعَانِ قَالَ أَصْحَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ
قَالَ كَلَّآ إِنَّ مَعِىَ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ كَٱلطَّوْدِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ
قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَٰكِفِينَ
قَالُوا۟ بَلْ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا كَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ
فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِّىٓ إِلَّا رَبَّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
وَٱلَّذِىٓ أَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لِى خَطِيٓـَٔتِى يَوْمَ ٱلدِّينِ
رَبِّ هَبْ لِى حُكْمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
وَٱجْعَل لِّى لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
وَٱغْفِرْ لِأَبِىٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ
إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى ٱللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ
وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ
مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ هَلْ يَنصُرُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَنتَصِرُونَ
تَٱللَّهِ إِن كُنَّا لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ نُوحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
قَالَ وَمَا عِلْمِى بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
إِنْ حِسَابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّى لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ
قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰنُوحُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَرْجُومِينَ
فَٱفْتَحْ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًا وَنَجِّنِى وَمَن مَّعِىَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ
إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ هُودٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
قَالُوا۟ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْنَآ أَوَعَظْتَ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْوَٰعِظِينَ
فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَهْلَكْنَٰهُمْ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ صَٰلِحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
ٱلَّذِينَ يُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ
مَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُنَا فَأْتِ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
قَالَ هَٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةٌ لَّهَا شِرْبٌ وَلَكُمْ شِرْبُ يَوْمٍ مَّعْلُومٍ
وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوٓءٍ فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ لُوطٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ عَادُونَ
قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰلُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْرَجِينَ
وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
أَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْسِرِينَ
وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا۟ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ
وَمَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُنَا وَإِن نَّظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ ٱلظُّلَّةِ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
أَوَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ ءَايَةً أَن يَعْلَمَهُۥ عُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
فَقَرَأَهُۥ عَلَيْهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ مُؤْمِنِينَ
لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ
مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يُمَتَّعُونَ
وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا لَهَا مُنذِرُونَ
فَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُعَذَّبِينَ
وَٱخْفِضْ جَنَاحَكَ لِمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
فَإِنْ عَصَوْكَ فَقُلْ إِنِّى بَرِىٓءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن تَنَزَّلُ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ
أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍ يَهِيمُونَ
إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَذَكَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَٱنتَصَرُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا۟ وَسَيَعْلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَىَّ مُنقَلَبٍ يَنقَلِبُونَ

leads.title: Utnapishtim's flood (Gilgamesh, Standard Babylonian Tablet XI:8-206) ↔ Noah, the lowly followers and the laden ark
leads.summary: 2 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

passages.text: (18:25) וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ לִנְבִיאֵ֣י הַבַּ֗עַל בַּחֲר֨וּ לָכֶ֜ם הַפָּ֤ר הָֽאֶחָד֙ וַעֲשׂ֣וּ רִאשֹׁנָ֔ה כִּ֥י אַתֶּ֖ם הָרַבִּ֑ים וְקִרְאוּ֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖שׁ לֹ֥א תָשִֽׂימוּ (18:26) וַ֠יִּקְחוּ אֶת הַפָּ֨ר אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֣ן לָהֶם֮ וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֒ וַיִּקְרְא֣וּ בְשֵׁם הַ֠בַּעַל מֵהַבֹּ֨קֶר וְעַד הַצָּהֳרַ֤יִם לֵאמֹר֙ הַבַּ֣עַל עֲנֵ֔נוּ וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל וְאֵ֣ין עֹנֶ֑ה וַֽיְפַסְּח֔וּ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה (18:27) וַיְהִ֨י בַֽצָּהֳרַ֜יִם וַיְהַתֵּ֧ל בָּהֶ֣ם אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ קִרְא֤וּ בְקוֹל גָּדוֹל֙ כִּֽי אֱלֹהִ֣ים ה֔וּא כִּ֣י שִׂ֧יחַ וְכִֽי שִׂ֛יג ל֖וֹ וְכִֽי דֶ֣רֶךְ ל֑וֹ אוּלַ֛י יָשֵׁ֥ן ה֖וּא וְיִקָֽץ (18:28) וַֽיִּקְרְאוּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וַיִּתְגֹּֽדְדוּ֙ כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔ם בַּחֲרָב֖וֹת וּבָֽרְמָחִ֑ים עַד שְׁפָךְ דָּ֖ם עֲלֵיהֶֽם (18:29) וַֽיְהִי֙ כַּעֲבֹ֣ר הַֽצָּהֳרַ֔יִם וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֔וּ עַ֖ד לַעֲל֣וֹת הַמִּנְחָ֑ה וְאֵֽין ק֥וֹל וְאֵין עֹנֶ֖ה וְאֵ֥ין קָֽשֶׁב

וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ אֶל כָּל הָעָ֗ם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ עַד מָתַ֞י אַתֶּ֣ם פֹּסְחִים֮ עַל שְׁתֵּ֣י הַסְּעִפִּים֒ אִם יְהוָ֤ה הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְכ֣וּ אַחֲרָ֔יו וְאִם הַבַּ֖עַל לְכ֣וּ אַחֲרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא עָנ֥וּ הָעָ֛ם אֹת֖וֹ דָּבָֽר
וּקְרָאתֶ֞ם בְּשֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֗ם וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶקְרָ֣א בְשֵׁם יְהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֧ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר יַעֲנֶ֥ה בָאֵ֖שׁ ה֣וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֧עַן כָּל הָעָ֛ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָֽר
قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ
قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ

leads.title: The basket of summer fruit; cheating merchants; famine of the word ↔ Shuayb and the People of the Thicket; the day of the canopy
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded (weight 5.3). Pair score 5.3.

Only in The basket of summer fruit; cheating merchants; famine of the word: Vision of a basket of summer fruit (qayits) means 'the end (qets) has come'; A famine not of bread or thirst for water, but of hearing the words of YHWH; they wander from sea to sea seeking it; Those who swear by the Ashimah of Samaria, 'As your god lives, O Dan', and 'As the way of Beersheba lives'; The whole land heaves and sinks like the Nile of Egypt; Merchants ask when the new moon and sabbath will be over so they can sell grain with small ephah, big shekel and false scales; God will make it like the mourning for an only son, with sackcloth and baldness; They sell the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals; God will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight; God asks the prophet 'What do you see?' and interprets the ordinary object he names.

Only in Shuayb and the People of the Thicket; the day of the canopy: Unbelievers challenge the prophet to make pieces of the sky fall on them; The People of the Thicket are destroyed by the punishment of the Day of the Canopy/Shadow (yawm al-ẓulla); Shuʿayb commands full measure and weighing with the straight balance, and not defrauding people; The people say the prophet is one of the bewitched and a mere human like them, and demand a sign; Shuʿayb is sent to the People of the Thicket (aṣḥāb al-ayka); No two kinds of weights or measures; just weights for long life; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'; The Prophet asks no wage for the message.

Shared motifs, rarest first: How God's word reaches the prophet [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Divination, soothsaying, mediums (ov) and wizards (yidde'oni) are forbidden (weight 6.8). Pair score 14.6.

Only in Levitical dues; forbidden divination; the prophet like Moses: Be wholehearted (tamim) with God; A prophecy that does not come true shows the prophet spoke presumptuously; Priest's due: shoulder, two cheeks and stomach of the sacrifice, and first of the fleece; Duty to accept a prophet God will send later [divergence between the texts]; A future prophet promised in the earlier scripture [response between the texts]; A future prophet 'from among them' [divergence between the texts]; Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them [contrast between the texts]; Whether the dead may be consulted, or would persuade the living if they spoke [contrast between the texts]; False prophet put to death [divergence between the texts]; God sent before only men, inspired, from the people of the towns; Messengers are sent to people from among themselves; People fear to hear God directly and ask the prophet to mediate; and 8 more.

Only in The Trustworthy Spirit, the scriptures of the ancients, devils, kin and poets: Devils did not bring down the revelation; they are barred from overhearing heaven; The devils descend upon every sinful liar, passing on what they overhear, mostly lies; Poets are followed by the deluded, wander in every valley and say what they do not do, except the believing poets; The Quran is in the scriptures (zubur) of the ancients and known to the learned of the Children of Israel; The Trustworthy Spirit (al-rūḥ al-amīn) brought the revelation down upon the prophet's heart; The prophet is told to warn his nearest kinsfolk; Ghosts and familiar spirits 'chirp and mutter'; 'should a people consult the dead on behalf of the living?'; Had it been revealed to a non-Arab (aʿjamī) reciting it, they would still not believe; God's spirit in relation to a person's heart [divergence between the texts]; 'Ask the people of the Reminder (ahl al-dhikr) if you do not know': appeal to earlier scripture-holders; False prophets prophesy 'from their own heart', following their own spirit, having seen nothing; God's 'holy spirit' (ruah qodesh) is asked not to be taken away from a person; and 2 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); How the sea was split for the crossing [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people (weight 7.7); Whether those who saw the sea miracle believed [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); King regrets releasing the slaves and pursues them with chariots (weight 7.3); 'Stand still and see the salvation of YHWH; YHWH will fight for you' (weight 7.3); Prophet stretches his staff over the sea and God splits it with a strong east wind (weight 6.8); The people walk on dry ground through the sea with the waters as a wall on either side (weight 6.4); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 5.5). Pair score 64.4.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; and 12 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; The king of Egypt as a god who has no second / no other god [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; and 42 more.

units.title: The pursuit and the parting of the sea

matches.label: Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites
matches.note: Motive for the pursuit: Exodus gives Pharaoh's regret (mah zōʾt ʿāśînû kî šillaḥnû ʾet Yiśrāʾēl mēʿovdēnû) and God hardening his heart so he will pursue and God be glorified (wə-ḥizzaqtî ʾet lēv Parʿōh wə-rādaf ʾaḥărêhem wə-ʾikkāvədâ bə-Farʿōh); Q 26:52 says only that God warned Moses 'innakum muttabaʿūn', and 26:54-55 gives Pharaoh's contempt (la-shirdhimatun qalīlūna ... la-ghāʾiẓūn). There is no regret over losing slaves and no hardening.

passages.text: וְחִזַּקְתִּ֣י אֶת לֵב פַּרְעֹה֮ וְרָדַ֣ף אַחֲרֵיהֶם֒ וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל חֵיל֔וֹ וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵֽן
וַיֻּגַּד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח הָעָ֑ם וַ֠יֵּהָפֵךְ לְבַ֨ב פַּרְעֹ֤ה וַעֲבָדָיו֙ אֶל הָעָ֔ם וַיֹּֽאמרוּ֙ מַה זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֔ינוּ כִּֽי שִׁלַּ֥חְנוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעָבְדֵֽנוּ
וַיְחַזֵּ֣ק יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶת לֵ֤ב פַּרְעֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּרְדֹּ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יֹצְאִ֖ים בְּיָ֥ד רָמָֽה
وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِىٓ إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ
فَأَرْسَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
فَأَتْبَعُوهُم مُّشْرِقِينَ

matches.label: How the sea was split for the crossing

matches.label: Whether those who saw the sea miracle believed
matches.note: Ending of the sea story: Exod 14:31 wa-yyîrəʾû hā-ʿām ʾet YHWH wa-yyaʾămînû ba-YHWH û-və-Mōše ʿavdô, the people believe, and the Song follows (15:1). The Quran's refrain: inna fī dhālika la-āyatan wa-mā kāna aktharuhum muʾminīna, a sign, yet most of them did not believe. Faith at the sea becomes unbelief despite the sign, aimed at the Quran's own audience.

matches.note: fa-arsala Firʿawnu fī l-madāʾini ḥāshirīna ~ wa-yyeʾsōr ʾet rikbô wə-ʾet ʿammô lāqaḥ ʿimmô wa-yyiqqaḥ šēš mēʾôt rekhev bāḥûr: Pharaoh musters his force; Exodus counts chariots, the Quran sends heralds to the cities.

וַיִּקַּ֗ח שֵׁשׁ מֵא֥וֹת רֶ֨כֶב֙ בָּח֔וּר וְכֹ֖ל רֶ֣כֶב מִצְרָ֑יִם וְשָׁלִשִׁ֖ם עַל כֻּלּֽוֹ

leads.title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses' upbringing in Pharaoh's house [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Hero flees the king's death sentence to a foreign land (weight 6.8). Pair score 21.9.

Only in Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry: The foundling's weeping moves the finder to compassion; The hero's parents are introduced anonymously as a Levite man and a Levite woman; Mother sees that her newborn 'is good' (ki tov); Hero names his son for being a stranger in a foreign land; Infant adopted by a royal woman [divergence between the texts]; The groaning of the oppressed rises to God, who hears and remembers his covenant; Hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand; Hero drives off shepherds and waters the flock of women at a well; How Moses learns that his life is sought [divergence between the texts]; How Moses killed the Egyptian [divergence between the texts]; What the Midianite daughters do after Moses helps them [divergence between the texts]; Moses helps the women at the water of Midian [divergence between the texts]; and 23 more.

matches.label: Moses' upbringing in Pharaoh's house
matches.note: a-lam nurabbika fīnā walīdan wa-labithta fīnā min ʿumurika sinīna ~ wat-təviʾēhû lə-vat Parʿōh wa-yhî lāh lə-vēn: Moses grew up in Pharaoh's house. Exodus credits Pharaoh's daughter and never has Pharaoh mention it; in the Quran Pharaoh himself throws the upbringing at Moses as a favor he is owed.

passages.text: וַיִגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֨הוּ֙ לְבַת פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מִן הַמַּ֖יִם מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ
قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ

matches.label: How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged
matches.note: The killing: Exod 2:12 wa-yyifen kōh wā-khōh wa-yyarʾ kî ʾên ʾîš wa-yyakh ʾet ham-Miṣrî wa-yyiṭmənēhû ba-ḥôl, deliberate and hidden, to defend a Hebrew (2:11); Q 26:20 faʿaltuhā idhan wa-ana mina ḍ-ḍāllīna, Moses admits he did it while 'astray', and Pharaoh calls him ungrateful (wa-anta mina l-kāfirīn). Exodus has no confession.

passages.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם וַיִּגְדַּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֶל אֶחָ֔יו וַיַּ֖רְא בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מַכֶּ֥ה אִישׁ עִבְרִ֖י מֵאֶחָֽיו
וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל
وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذًا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ

matches.label: Hero flees the king's death sentence to a foreign land
matches.note: fa-farartu minkum lammā khiftukum ~ wa-yyîrāʾ Mōše ... wa-yyivraḥ Mōše mip-pənê Farʿōh: fear (khāfa / yārēʾ) and flight (farra / bāraḥ). The Quran adds the outcome: fa-wahaba lī rabbī ḥukman wa-jaʿalanī mina l-mursalīn.

passages.text: וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ הַלְהָרְגֵ֨נִי֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֑י וַיִּירָ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע הַדָּבָֽר
וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לַהֲרֹ֣ג אֶת מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּבְרַ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ מִדְיָ֖ן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עַֽל הַבְּאֵֽר

matches.label: The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh
matches.note: The divine title before Pharaoh: YHWH ʾĕlōhê hā-ʿivriyyîm niqrâ ʿālênû (Exod 3:18, also 5:3) ~ innā rasūlu rabbi l-ʿālamīna, and when Pharaoh asks 'and what is the Lord of the worlds?', Moses answers rabbu s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi wa-mā baynahumā ... rabbu l-mashriqi wa-l-maghribi. The god of one people becomes the Lord of the cosmos.

passages.text: וְשָׁמְע֖וּ לְקֹלֶ֑ךָ וּבָאתָ֡ אַתָּה֩ וְזִקְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֗יִם וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָֽעִבְרִיִּים֙ נִקְרָ֣ה עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְעַתָּ֗ה נֵֽלֲכָה נָּ֞א דֶּ֣רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְנִזְבְּחָ֖ה לַֽיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ

قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ

matches.label: Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story
matches.note: 'God of your fathers' changes addressee. Exod 3:15, said to Israel: YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾăvōtêkem ʾĕlōhê ʾAvrāhām ʾĕlōhê Yiṣḥāq wē-ʾlōhê Yaʿăqōv. Q 26:26, said to Pharaoh and his court: rabbukum wa-rabbu ābāʾikumu l-awwalīna, 'your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers'. The God of Israel's ancestors becomes the Lord of the Egyptians' ancestors too.

matches.note: God's answer to Moses' reluctance: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... hălōʾ ʾAhărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wə-ʾattâ tihyeh lô lēʾlōhîm (anger; Aaron as mouth, Moses as God to him) ~ qāla kallā fa-dhhabā bi-āyātinā innā maʿakum mustamiʿūna: no anger and no 'as God'; both are sent as equals (fa-dhhabā, dual).

passages.text: וַיִּֽחַר אַ֨ף יְהוָ֜ה בְּמֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֨יךָ֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי דַבֵּ֥ר יְדַבֵּ֖ר ה֑וּא וְגַ֤ם הִנֵּה הוּא֙ יֹצֵ֣א לִקְרָאתֶ֔ךָ וְרָאֲךָ֖ וְשָׂמַ֥ח בְּלִבּֽוֹ
וְדִבֶּר ה֥וּא לְךָ֖ אֶל הָעָ֑ם וְהָ֤יָה הוּא֙ יִֽהְיֶה לְּךָ֣ לְפֶ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶה לּ֥וֹ לֵֽאלֹהִֽים
وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ

matches.label: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death
matches.note: Fear of being killed for the old killing: in Exodus God removes it by fact, kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā; in the Quran Moses raises it himself (wa-lahum ʿalayya dhanbun fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni), and God answers with his presence, 'kallā ... innā maʿakum mustamiʿūn'.

matches.label: Moses' hand turned white as a sign
matches.note: wa-nazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāʾu li-n-nāẓirīna ~ wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: the white hand. In Exodus it is leprous (məṣōraʿat), shown to Moses at the bush and meant for the Israelites (4:8-9, 4:30); in the Quran it is simply 'white for the beholders', shown to Pharaoh and his court, with no disease.

passages.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ ע֗וֹד הָֽבֵא נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּבֵ֥א יָד֖וֹ בְּחֵיק֑וֹ וַיּ֣וֹצִאָ֔הּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה יָד֖וֹ מְצֹרַ֥עַת כַּשָּֽׁלֶג
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הָשֵׁ֤ב יָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל חֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּ֥שֶׁב יָד֖וֹ אֶל חֵיק֑וֹ וַיּֽוֹצִאָהּ֙ מֵֽחֵיק֔וֹ וְהִנֵּה שָׁ֖בָה כִּבְשָׂרֽוֹ
وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

matches.label: Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips'
matches.note: wa-yaḍīqu ṣadrī wa-lā yanṭaliqu lisānī fa-arsil ilā Hārūna ~ kî khəvad peh û-khəvad lāšôn ʾānōkhî ... šəlaḥ nāʾ bə-yad tišlāḥ: Moses' tongue (lisān / lāšôn) is not free, and he asks God to send someone else. In the Quran he names Aaron himself.

וַיֹּ֖אמֶר בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑י שְֽׁלַֽח נָ֖א בְּיַד תִּשְׁלָֽח

وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Salih, the rock-hewn houses of Thamud and the she-camel
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: How a people responds to a sign given to prove the messenger [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.

Only in Salih, the rock-hewn houses of Thamud and the she-camel: The people say the prophet is one of the bewitched and a mere human like them, and demand a sign; The prophet Ṣāliḥ is sent to the people of Thamūd; Thamūd hew houses out of the mountains, among gardens, springs and palms with tender spathes; Edom dwells in the clefts of the rock (sela) and thinks no one can bring it down; The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; The unbelievers demand: 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?'; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'.

matches.label: How a people responds to a sign given to prove the messenger
matches.note: fa-ʾti bi-āyatin in kunta mina ṣ-ṣādiqīna qāla hādhihi nāqatun ... fa-ʿaqarūhā ~ wə-hēn lōʾ yaʾămînû lî ... wə-heʾĕmînû lə-qōl hā-ʾōt hā-ʾaḥărôn ... wa-yyaʾămēn hā-ʿām: a sign (āya / ʾôt) given to prove the messenger. In Exodus the signs win the people's faith; Thamūd demand a sign, receive the she-camel, and kill it.

passages.text: וַיַּ֤עַן מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר וְהֵן֙ לֹֽא יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לִ֔י וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְע֖וּ בְּקֹלִ֑י כִּ֣י יֹֽאמְר֔וּ לֹֽא נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה
וְהָיָה֙ אִם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לָ֔ךְ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וְהֶֽאֱמִ֔ינוּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֥ת הָאַחֲרֽוֹן
וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ כִּֽי פָקַ֨ד יְהוָ֜ה אֶת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְכִ֤י רָאָה֙ אֶת עָנְיָ֔ם וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ
مَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُنَا فَأْتِ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
قَالَ هَٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةٌ لَّهَا شِرْبٌ وَلَكُمْ شِرْبُ يَوْمٍ مَّعْلُومٍ
فَعَقَرُوهَا فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ نَٰدِمِينَ

leads.title: First audience with Pharaoh; bricks without straw ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Pharaoh's question about, or claim to know, the god of Moses [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' (weight 7.3); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' (weight 6.5). Pair score 21.2.

Only in First audience with Pharaoh; bricks without straw: Slaves must make the same quota of bricks while gathering their own straw; The oppressed blame the deliverer for making things worse; Prophet complains to God that his mission has only made things worse; Foreign taskmasters over native foremen who are beaten for unmet quotas; Tyrant accuses the oppressed of idleness for wanting to worship; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh gathers the people and proclaims 'I am your Lord most high' [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh: 'I show you only what I see, and guide you only to the right path'; Request for a three days' journey into the wilderness to sacrifice; King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' [divergence between the texts]; Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' [divergence between the texts]; Unbelievers defend their practice as what they found their fathers doing.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; The king of Egypt as a god who has no second / no other god [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; and 48 more.

matches.label: Pharaoh's question about, or claim to know, the god of Moses
matches.note: Pharaoh's question about the god: mî YHWH ʾăšer ʾešmaʿ bə-qōlô ... lōʾ yādaʿtî ʾet YHWH ~ wa-mā rabbu l-ʿālamīna. In Exodus Moses gives no answer and God answers through the plagues (so that Egypt will know, 7:5); in the Quran Moses answers at once in a three-step creed (Lord of heavens and earth, your Lord and your fathers' Lord, Lord of east and west), and Pharaoh mocks him to his court as mad (la-majnūn).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֔ה מִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶשְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹל֔וֹ לְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹ֤א יָדַ֨עְתִּי֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה וְגַ֥ם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א אֲשַׁלֵּֽחַ
قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ
قَالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُۥٓ أَلَا تَسْتَمِعُونَ

matches.label: Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me'
matches.note: an arsil maʿanā banī Isrāʾīla ~ šallaḥ ʾet ʿammî: the same verb 'send away / release' (arsala / šillaḥ). Exodus says it in the prophetic formula kōh ʾāmar YHWH ʾĕlōhê Yiśrāʾēl and adds wə-yāḥōggû lî ba-mmidbār; the Quran's speakers are messengers of the Lord of the worlds.

passages.text: וְאַחַ֗ר בָּ֚אוּ מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֑ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שַׁלַּח֙ אֶת עַמִּ֔י וְיָחֹ֥גּוּ לִ֖י בַּמִּדְבָּֽר
فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

matches.label: What the sin of Lot's townsmen was
matches.note: The sin: Genesis has one night's event, the townsmen demanding Lot's two guests, hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wə-nēdəʿâ ʾōtām; the Quran has a standing practice of the whole people, a-taʾtūna dh-dhukrāna mina l-ʿālamīna wa-tadharūna mā khalaqa lakum rabbukum min azwājikum. Shared motifs, rarest first: The Day of YHWH: a coming day of divine judgment, terror and darkness (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in The mountain of the Lord's house; the Day of YHWH against all that is proud: Stop trusting man, who has only breath in his nostrils; On that day people throw their silver and gold idols to the moles and bats and flee into clefts of the rocks; Foreign priests and diviners advise how to appease the God of Israel; In the latter days the mountain of God's house will be raised above all mountains and all nations will stream to it; When God's help and the opening (al-fath) come, people enter God's religion in crowds; the prophet is to glorify and seek forgiveness; 'From Zion shall go forth Torah and the word of YHWH from Jerusalem'; God shatters the ships of Tarshish with an east wind; God the Judge is called to judge between two nations; On God's day all that is lofty (cedars of Lebanon, oaks of Bashan, towers, ships of Tarshish) is brought low and God alone exalted; People hide in caves, thickets, rocks and pits from an invading army; Nations will beat swords into plowshares and spears into pruning hooks and learn war no more; On the day of judgment voices are hushed before the Merciful; only a faint murmur is heard; and 2 more.

Only in Hud and the monument-building people of Ad: The people of ʿĀd build a monument on every height and take fortresses (maṣāniʿ) hoping to live forever; Their graves (qirbam = qivram) are their houses forever, though they named lands after themselves; The prophet Hūd is sent to the people of ʿĀd; Monuments built so that their builders may live for ever [neutral]; Men build great structures to endure, but the builders and their buildings pass [divergence between the texts]; Nimrod, first mighty man, a mighty hunter before the LORD; Building with baked bricks and bitumen instead of stone and mortar; Woe to the one who builds a city (Zion) with bloodshed and injustice; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal; Builders seek to make a name for themselves and avoid dispersal; and 2 more.

leads.title: Valley of vision; let us eat and drink; Shebna deposed, Eliakim given the key of David ↔ Salih, the rock-hewn houses of Thamud and the she-camel
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Thamūd hew houses out of the mountains, among gardens, springs and palms with tender spathes (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Valley of vision; let us eat and drink; Shebna deposed, Eliakim given the key of David: Revelers say 'Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die' when called to mourning; God will wind the official up and hurl him like a ball into a wide land, where he and his glorious chariots will die; Successor clothed with the predecessor's robe and sash and given his authority; God places the key of the house of David on the new steward's shoulder: what he opens none shall shut, what he shuts none shall open; Official fastened like a peg in a secure place on which his family's honor hangs; the peg will later give way; Prophet: 'Look away from me, let me weep bitterly; do not try to comfort me over the ruin of my people'; City prepares for siege (armory of the House of the Forest, counting houses, tearing them down for the wall, a reservoir between walls) but does not look to its Maker; The steward Shebna, 'over the house', rebuked for hewing himself a lofty tomb in the rock; God swears this iniquity will not be atoned for until they die; Oracle on 'the valley of vision' (Jerusalem) whose people revel on rooftops while the day of tumult comes; Who holds the keys that open and shut [divergence between the texts]; King makes a pool and conduit to bring water into the city; and 2 more.

Only in Salih, the rock-hewn houses of Thamud and the she-camel: The people say the prophet is one of the bewitched and a mere human like them, and demand a sign; How a people responds to a sign given to prove the messenger [contrast between the texts]; The prophet Ṣāliḥ is sent to the people of Thamūd; Edom dwells in the clefts of the rock (sela) and thinks no one can bring it down; The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; The unbelievers demand: 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?'; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'.

leads.title: Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm ↔ Abraham's argument against idols and his prayer
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: On that day neither wealth nor sons avail, only one who comes to God with a sound heart (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm: Speaker laments that in the noon of his days he must go to the gates of Sheol, deprived of the rest of his years; A psalm-like 'writing' (mikhtav) of the king composed when he was sick and recovered; My dwelling is pulled up like a shepherd's tent; I have rolled up my life like a weaver, he cuts me off from the loom; God has cast all the speaker's sins behind his back and held back his soul from the pit of destruction; The dead cannot praise God: no wonders for the dead, no hesed in the grave, no faithfulness in Abaddon; A dying person's plea to God for more life, and God's answer [contrast between the texts]; A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king; Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward); Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die'; Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping; Bequest (wasiyya) to parents and kin prescribed for one who leaves wealth; altering it is a sin; In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life; and 5 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

passages.text: قَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ
إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ

sides.note: they also say Pharaoh compelled them to practise sorcery

passages.text: قَالُوا۟ لَا ضَيْرَ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ
إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَآ أَن كُنَّآ أَوَّلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

sides.note: 'no harm; to our Lord we return'

matches.label: The magicians' ropes and staffs appear by sorcery to be moving like snakes

passages.text: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا۟ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ
فَأَلْقَوْا۟ حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا۟ بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ

matches.label: King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?'

passages.text: قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ

sides.note: 'Who then is the Lord of you two, Moses?'

passages.text: قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

sides.note: 'And what is the Lord of the worlds?'

matches.label: The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron

passages.text: فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ
فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سَٰجِدِينَ
قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
رَبِّ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ

matches.label: The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents

passages.text: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَٰحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ
فَأَلْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ
فَأَلْقَوْا۟ حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا۟ بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ

matches.label: Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me'

passages.text: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ قَدْ جِئْنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ

sides.note: 'send the children of Israel with us and do not torment them'

passages.text: فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ

matches.label: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest

passages.text: قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِّثْلِهِۦ فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّا نُخْلِفُهُۥ نَحْنُ وَلَآ أَنتَ مَكَانًا سُوًى
فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ
قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ
قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ

leads.title: Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven ↔ Noah, the lowly followers and the laden ark
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.8); Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents (weight 6.5); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood (weight 6.2); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). Pair score 32.3.

Only in Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven: God forbids the prophet to address him on behalf of those who did wrong: they will be drowned; The flood hero prays to be landed at a blessed landing place; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; The flood hero is told he is only a man like the speaker(s) [divergence between the texts]; When and from where the flood waters come [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; The flood waters are hot or boiling; Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts]; A member of the hero's family is lost; A specific sign marks the moment to board; Animals taken aboard in pairs; Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction; and 1 more.

Only in Noah, the lowly followers and the laden ark: The people threaten to stone the prophet if he does not desist; The hero is saved with those with him in the laden ark (al-fulk al-mashḥūn); The prophet's opponents object that only the lowliest follow him; he refuses to drive the believers away; Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [contrast between the texts]; The people are about to stone their leader; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'; All others perish; The Prophet asks no wage for the message.

matches.label: Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood

passages.text: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَقَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةً مَّا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌۢ بِهِۦ جِنَّةٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ

sides.note: In Genesis Noah never speaks before the flood: wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô; he is chosen because God saw him righteous (ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq). In the Quran he is a messenger (arsalnā Nūḥan ilā qawmihi) who preaches 'yā qawmi ʿbudū llāha mā lakum min ilāhin ghayruhu', and the chiefs answer that he is only a man like them, possessed (bihi jinna).

passages.text: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ نُوحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ
فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ

sides.note: Genesis' Noah obeys in silence (wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô ʾĕlōhîm) and is never sent to anyone; the Quran's Noah is 'their brother' and 'a trustworthy messenger' (akhūhum ... rasūlun amīn) who asks no wage, and his people 'denied the messengers' (kadhdhabat qawmu Nūḥin al-mursalīn).

matches.label: Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why

passages.text: فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

sides.note: Genesis saves the whole household, bōʾ ʾattâ wə-khol bêtəkā ... Nōaḥ û-vānāyw wə-ʾištô û-nəšê vānāyw; the Quran excepts some: wa-ahlaka illā man sabaqa ʿalayhi l-qawlu minhum (the drowned son of 11:42-43), and forbids Noah to plead for the wrongdoers (wa-lā tukhāṭibnī fī lladhīna ẓalamū).

passages.text: فَٱفْتَحْ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًا وَنَجِّنِى وَمَن مَّعِىَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ

sides.note: Who is saved with Noah: Genesis, his household for his own righteousness, bōʾ ʾattâ wə-khol bêtəkā ... kî ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq (Noah, his sons, his wife, his sons' wives); Quran, najjinī wa-man maʿiya mina l-muʾminīna ... fa-anjaynāhu wa-man maʿahu fī l-fulki l-mashḥūn, the believers who followed him, the 'lowliest' (al-ardhalūn, 26:111). The saved group is defined by faith, not by kinship.

leads.title: Lot and his people ↔ Lot and the people who expel the pure
leads.summary: 7 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Lot condemns his people for approaching males and leaving the wives God created for them (weight 7.7); The town that was rained on with an evil rain (Lot's) is passed by travelers (weight 7.3); Lot's people threaten to expel him (weight 7.3); The fate of Lot's wife (weight 6.8); Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt (weight 6.6); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 5.9); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). Pair score 47.2.

Only in Lot and his people: Lot's family is saved except an old woman among those who stayed behind; What the sin of Lot's townsmen was [divergence between the texts]; Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts]; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'; The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked.

Only in Lot and the people who expel the pure: Lot's people mock his family as 'people who keep themselves pure' and order their expulsion; What Lot says to the townsmen [divergence between the texts]; Lot's townspeople turn on him [divergence between the texts].

passages.text: أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلذُّكْرَانَ مِنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ عَادُونَ
وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ

passages.text: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

passages.text: قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰلُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْرَجِينَ
فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَخْرِجُوٓا۟ ءَالَ لُوطٍ مِّن قَرْيَتِكُمْ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ

matches.label: The fate of Lot's wife

passages.text: إِلَّا عَجُوزًا فِى ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

sides.note: illā ʿajūzan fī l-ghābirīna ~ wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ: the one family member lost. Genesis names her Lot's wife and says why (she looked back) and how (pillar of salt); the Quran says only 'an old woman among those who stayed behind', with no looking back and no salt.

passages.text: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَٰهَا مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

sides.note: Who decides the wife's fate: Genesis gives her own act, the warning ʾal tabbîṭ ʾaḥărêkā and wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ; the Quran gives God's decree, illā mraʾatahu qaddarnāhā mina l-ghābirīna, 'we decreed her among those who stayed behind', with no looking back and no salt.

passages.text: وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

sides.note: Why Egypt refuses: Exod 8:15 the magicians admit ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm hîʾ, yet wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh ... ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart is hardened as God foretold; Q 27:14 wa-jaḥadū bihā wa-staiqanathā anfusuhum ẓulman wa-ʿuluwwan, they rejected the signs though inwardly convinced, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The court magicians ask the king for a reward if they win and are promised closeness (weight 7.7); The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron (weight 7.3); The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents (weight 7.1); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 6.6); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' (weight 6.5); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 6.5); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 6.0); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 5.5). Only in Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues: Pharaoh's people are struck with years of drought and lack of fruits before the plagues; Enemies attribute their misfortune to the prophet as a bad omen (tatayyur); their omen is with God; The magicians' spell bewitches the people's eyes and terrifies them; The magicians offer the prophet to throw first; he tells them to throw; Pharaoh is said to have his own gods, whom Moses would make him abandon; One of the Egyptian plagues is a flood (tufan); The tyrant threatens to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify the converts; Taking or reading an omen from birds is set aside; Blood comes upon Egypt as a calamity [divergence between the texts]; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [contrast between the texts]; An Egyptian ruler moves to kill the children (sons) of one who stirs up the land [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; What the defeated magician says and what is done to him [divergence between the texts]; and 27 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; The king of Egypt as a god who has no second / no other god [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; and 43 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 6.5); Vessel comes to rest on a named mountain (weight 6.4); Hero singled out as righteous or pious (weight 6.2); Waters pour both from the sky and from springs of the earth (weight 6.2); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 6.2); Deity decides to destroy humankind (weight 6.1); All others perish (weight 5.9); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.8); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). Pair score 54.8.

Only in Noah in the Quran: Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; Vessel described by its planks and fastenings; The flood waters are hot or boiling; Hero's life or mission spans 950 years; A member of the hero's family is lost; A specific sign marks the moment to board; People mock the hero while he builds the vessel; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Hero blessed on leaving the vessel; Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer [divergence between the texts]; How the ark is described [divergence between the texts]; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; and 37 more.

وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَٰحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ
فَأَلْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ
